Folks — draft technical breakdown below. Sharing both conservative baseline and a tighter paid option so the commercial team can frame pricing.

Baseline (included):
- RTO (time to resume request routing to a secondary region): best-effort within 60–180 minutes depending on customer session patterns and cross-region capacity at the time. We target 99.95% per-region availability under normal conditions.
- RPO (data loss tolerance): asynchronous replication, typical RPO <= 15 minutes for embeddings/metadata. For session-level ephemeral state (KV cache) RPO is "best-effort" — we recommend application-level checkpoints for critical transactions.
- Client-visible latency delta during first hour after failover: expect a 150–350 ms median increase for requests that miss warmed KV/prefix cache; tail can be higher for long-context flows while KV cache warms. We quantify this as an "attenuation window" rather than an SLA breach.

Priority failover (paid add-on):
- Guaranteed activation lead time: 30 minutes for routing cutover and reserved warm capacity; contractually backed.
- RPO: still asynchronous replication but we provide accelerated cache-warming by pre-allocating prefix warmers and session affinity proxies — reduces median latency delta to 40–80 ms.
- Pricing: add-on charged as a monthly reserved standby fee + per-activation credit. (Commercial to propose exact numbers.)

Notes / implementation caveats:
- Warm cache effectiveness is workload dependent. If ClearWave has high unique session churn per user, warmers help less. We should include a small sample of their traffic (prefix distribution) to model actual delta.
- Cross-region DNS TTLs and client-side retries matter for observed RTO. Recommend short TTL during PoC (30s) while testing; procurement usually wants higher TTLs in prod.
- Failover choreography: our control plane will attempt automated routing within configured windows; if warm capacity not available we fall back to best-effort (longer RTO). We can bake deterministic fallback tiers into the SOW.

I've attached a simple SLA-diff table (SLA-failover-diff-table.xlsx) and a proposed paragraph for the contract. Kimberly: see last section for commercial phrasing suggestion.

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a concise proposal and the SLA diff table Karthik referenced. High level:

1) Baseline (included in standard hosting):
- Per-region uptime target: 99.95% monthly.
- Failover activation: best-effort 60–180 minutes; we commit to automated routing attempts and operational playbooks.
- RPO: asynchronous replication, targeted <= 15 minutes for persistent artifacts; ephemeral cache advised to be checkpointed by the app.
- Client impact: expect an initial latency delta ("attenuation window") of ~150–350 ms median during the first hour while caches warm; we treat this as operational behavior not an SLA breach.

2) Priority failover (optional add-on):
- Guaranteed activation lead time: <= 30 minutes (SLA-backed).
- Improved client latency profile: median delta reduced to ~40–80 ms via pre-warmed capacity and accelerated cache-warmers.
- Commercial model: monthly reserved standby fee + per-activation credit. Proposed numbers are in the attached proposal.

3) Practical alignment items for procurement/SecOps:
- We'll run a short traffic sampling exercise to quantify expected attenuation for ClearWave's actual prefixes.
- Recommend temporarily setting short DNS TTL during PoC validation to confirm RTO numbers; will revert to longer TTL for production with agreed-upon windows.
- Add a runbook appendix that lists escalation contacts, activation checklist, and observability hooks (we included in the PDF).

If this aligns with your expectation, Kimberly will prepare SOW language and the DocuSign packet for signature. Happy to hop on a brief call to walk through the tradeoffs.
